nodes.summary: For every context-free language $L$ over an alphabet $T$ there are a context-free grammar $g$ over $T$ and a finitely supported pushdown automaton with input alphabet $T$, a single state, and the terminals and nonterminals of $g$ as stack alphabet, whose language accepted by empty stack is $L$.

nodes.title: Context-free languages are accepted by pushdown automata

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a pushdown automaton with a finite set of states and a finite stack alphabet, and suppose that there is a finite set $T_0$ of input letters such that $M$ has no transition, from any state and popping any stack symbol, that consumes a letter outside $T_0$. Then the language accepted by $M$ by empty stack is context-free.
nodes.title: Finite pushdown automata accept context-free languages

nodes.summary: A language $L$ over an alphabet $T$ is context-free if and only if there are a pushdown automaton $M$ over $T$ with a finite set of states and a finite stack alphabet, and a finite set $T_0$ of input letters such that $M$ has no transition, from any state and popping any stack symbol, that consumes a letter outside $T_0$, for which the language accepted by $M$ by empty stack is $L$.
nodes.title: Context-free languages are exactly the languages of finite pushdown automata

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a pushdown automaton with a finite set of states, a finite stack alphabet, start state $q_0$ and initial stack symbol $Z_0$, and let $T_0$ be a finite set of input letters. For every state $q$, the triple grammar of $M$ and $T_0$ contains the production $S \to (q_0, Z_0, q)$, where $S$ is its initial nonterminal.

Then the language generated by the triple grammar of $M$ and $T_0$ equals the language accepted by $M$ by empty stack.

nodes.title: Triple grammar of a pushdown automaton

nodes.summary: For a finite set $\sigma$ of states and a natural number $n$, this is the finite set of all lists of length $n$ with entries in $\sigma$. It is built recursively: for $n = 0$ it contains only the empty list, and for $n + 1$ it consists of the lists obtained by putting a state $p \in \sigma$ in front of a list from the set for $n$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
